event.title: fix(mcp): local server answers 500 when a request fails instead of crashing
event.author: predictable-code[bot]
event.body:
## Summary

`node:http` ignores the promise an async request handler returns. A throw inside the handler of `mcp/serve.ts` was an unhandled rejection, and on current Node that stops the process: one bad request killed the local MCP server (`npm run mcp:serve`).

```diff
 createHttpServer(async (req, res) =>
+  try
     parse the URL                      # throws on "GET //"
     if path is not /mcp: answer 404
     build the web Request              # throws on TRACE
     handle the MCP request, send the response
+  catch
+    log the error
+    answer 500, or end the response if the headers were already sent
```

Changed after review: the first version of this PR put the `try` below the URL parse, so `GET //` still stopped the server. The `try` now covers the whole handler.

Only the local development server changes. The Firebase function is untouched: `firebase-functions` already wraps its handler and answers 500.

## Evidence

Local server started with `tsx mcp/serve.ts`, Node 24.22.3:

| Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TRACE /mcp` | process stops | 500, server keeps running |
| `GET //` | process stops | 500, server keeps running |
| `GET /otra` | 404 | 404 |
| `POST /mcp` `initialize` | 200 | 200 |

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.mcp.json --noEmit`: no errors.
- `npm run test:mcp`: 2 files, 32 tests passed. No test covers `serve.ts` itself: it starts a server on import.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** local

Nothing published or deployed uses `mcp/serve.ts`. No real MCP client reaches the new `catch`: the SDK answers malformed MCP requests itself with a JSON-RPC error.
